summary: This division appears in the national court history of the anti-LGBT municipal-resolution wave: the provincial administrative court sitting in Gliwice ruled on the Istebna gmina resolution, and the Supreme Administrative Court's ruling of 28 June 2022 dismissed the appeals of four municipalities whose annulments had been ordered below, holding that the resolutions "violate the dignity" of LGBT people (an earlier May 2022 ruling held they "pose a risk of violence against LGBT people"). Otherwise no voivodeship-level trans-specific incident series or enforcement finding was located for this division in the current research pass — the municipal-resolution wave concentrated elsewhere. The national frame governs: no hate-crime protection on sexual-orientation or gender-identity grounds (the March 2025 amendment bill referred to the Constitutional Tribunal), court-based and medically gatekept legal gender recognition, and national sources documenting a trans foreign woman held in a male-only guarded detention centre and an ECtHR ruling that denying a prisoner hormone therapy violates private life.

sources.summary: Legal-aid NGO report (13-28 March 2024): a Polish regional court placed a Vietnamese trans woman, taking hormones since 2018, in a guarded detention centre for male foreigners; the Border Guard refused to move her or to deliver her medication, interrupting her hormone therapy for three months; she was released after the NGO's application citing health grounds (Act on Foreigners, Art. 406(1) with 400(1)).

TGEU report (16 July 2024): on 11 July the ECtHR held that Polish prison authorities violated the right to private and family life by denying a trans woman access to hormone replacement therapy while imprisoned (she had been prescribed hormones for almost two years; Siedlce prison gave no reasonable grounds for refusal); EUR 8,000 damages ordered; TGEU intervened in 2021; part of a growing Council of Europe standard on trans prisoners' healthcare.

NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (fetch failed); the underlying source is a case-law database entry for the same 2024 ECtHR judgment on denial of hormone therapy in prison reported by the second source.

outOfScopeNotes: Passport theft, overcharging by unlicensed taxis, and general urban crime affect all travellers here and are not trans-specific.
tangentialFactors: The national criminal-code amendment that would have added sexual-orientation and gender-identity hate-crime grounds remains suspended at the constitutional court, so all offences here are prosecuted without SOGI aggravation; the nationwide anti-LGBT municipal-declaration wave (80+ municipalities, concentrated in other voivodeships) shapes the surrounding climate even without a declaration in this division. The Istebna gmina resolution and its litigation history are recorded here as background of that wave.
localsOnly: The court-based, medically gatekept legal-gender-recognition regime is resident-facing; the ECtHR hormone-therapy ruling concerned a resident prisoner, and prison health provisions bind the state for residents and pre-trial detainees alike.
